correctness.rationale: For each k<=n, write Sn=Sk+(Sn-Sk); centered future independent of event {Sk>0}, so E[Sn 1(Sk>0)]=E[Sk 1(Sk>0)]=E|Sk|/2 by symmetry, valid for symmetric integrable increments even with ties. Summing gives exact covariance. With continuous iid symmetric increments Sparre–Andersen yields P(An=r)=binom(2r,r)binom(2n-2r,n-r)/4^n and Var An=n(n+1)/8, hence correlation sqrt(2)*sum E|Sk|/(sigma*n*sqrt(n+1)). CLT + bounded second moments ensure uniform integrability of |Sk|/(sigma sqrt k), giving limit 4/(3sqrt(pi)); Brownian identity by Fubini/conditional mean and Var Gamma=1/8. Independent exhaustive symmetric ±1 walks n<=11 confirmed the general covariance identity, not the continuous-increment arcsine marginal.
residual_risks: The finite-n beta-binomial marginal requires no atom at 0 (continuous increment law); discrete lattice ties are not covered by it. Correlation finite positive variance.

originality.rationale: The well-known Sparre–Andersen and Erdős–Kac laws are marginal sojourn-count laws and do not alone determine covariance with terminal displacement. Ivanovs discusses occupation-time distributions under endpoint conditioning, but its inspected propositions establish distributional identities between random times, not this first mixed moment or the all-symmetric-increment correlation constant. Brownian global-time joint laws address three times, not B1. The exact finite-n covariance for all symmetric integrable increments and universal finite-variance asymptotic survive best-of-knowledge comparison, though broad classical fluctuation literature poses residual overlap risk.
residual_risks: A much older full joint transform for (positive sojourn,terminal position) may imply this mixed moment even if absent from searched titles; do not claim a failed search proves novelty. Brownian standalone identity may be classical even if finite-n universality remains distinct.

value.rationale: Occupation fraction is a canonical arcsine functional, while terminal displacement is a canonical additive endpoint. Their exact finite-n mixed covariance and universal nonzero correlation 4/(3sqrt(pi)) quantify dependence that marginal arcsine and CLT statements leave undetermined. This is a motivated joint-statistic fact valid for a broad finite-variance universality class, not simply a renaming of the arcsine marginal.
residual_risks: Does not supply the full two-variable joint law; breadth of older fluctuation theory may affect priority.

limitations: Continuous law needed for finite beta-binomial A_n; exact covariance valid for symmetric integrable independent increments; finite nonzero variance for Pearson limit.
